post.summary: Ask for an artifact to be deleted after the grace period.
post.description: Ask for an artifact to be deleted: it is pending until its grace period (TANGIBLE_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS, 7 by default) ends, when its bytes are removed and its record kept, as a tombstone. Until then it can be kept. New burns, derivations and checks of it are refused meanwhile, and the RomM export stops using it. An original needs confirm_original. Refused with a retention lock, or while a burn, a derivation, a check or its import's source removal is queued or under way. Asking again while it is pending changes nothing. Needs an administrator, and is audited.

Reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID` (or `after`) replays what was missed while the server holds it; otherwise, or when the client falls behind, `stream.reset` is sent and the client should reconcile through the REST routes. # Errors

`NOT_FOUND` for an unknown worker.

put.description: Report what this worker and its drive can do, and receive the drive identifier to claim work with.

post.summary: Ask for work.
post.description: Ask for a burn job. Answers 204 when there is nothing to do.

post.summary: Issue a worker a new credential to replace the one it uses.
post.description: Issue this worker a new credential, returned once. The old credential keeps working until a request presents the new one, which then replaces it for good; asking again before that replaces the unused one. A worker asks when a heartbeat says `credential_rotation_required`, between jobs. Audited.

post.summary: Drain a worker: it finishes what it holds and takes nothing new.
post.description: Drain a worker: at its next heartbeat it is told to take no new work, and claims answer it with nothing to do, while what it holds runs to the end. Draining a draining worker changes nothing. Needs an administrator, and is audited.

post.summary: Undo a drain.
post.description: Undo a drain: the worker takes work again. Enabling a worker that is not draining changes nothing. Needs an administrator, and is audited.

post.summary: Ask for an erasure queued for this worker's drive.
post.description: Take the next erasure queued for this worker's drive. Answers 204 when there is none, or while a burn attempt holds the drive.

404.description: Not this worker, or not its drive

post.summary: Report that a worker is alive.
post.description: Report that a worker is alive and receive any instruction to stop taking new work.

post.summary: Reconcile a worker that restarted holding local state.
post.description: Reconcile a worker that restarted holding local state. No directive ever permits writing.

post.summary: Revoke a worker, for good.
post.description: Revoke a worker's credential, for good: its next request is refused, so it can no longer take work, renew a lease or report. An attempt it held lapses as a lost worker's does; nothing interrupts a write. To use the machine again, enroll it with a new token under a new name. Revoking a revoked worker changes nothing. Needs an administrator, and is audited.

post.summary: Ask for a rip queued for this worker's drive.
post.description: Take the next rip queued for this worker's drive. Answers 204 when there is none, or while a burn or an erasure holds the drive. Asked after erasure claims and before burn claims.

404.description: Not this worker, or not its drive

post.summary: Ask a worker to rotate its credential.
post.description: Ask a worker to rotate its credential: its next heartbeat says so, and it asks for a new one between jobs. The old credential keeps working until the worker first uses the new one, so nothing is interrupted. A worker too old to rotate keeps its credential and the request stays open; revoke it instead if the credential may be known to somebody else. Needs an administrator, and is audited.

get.description: Liveness. Answers whenever the process can serve a request and deliberately checks no dependency, so a database outage cannot cause a restart loop.

get.summary: Readiness probe: every dependency needed to serve traffic is usable.
get.description: Readiness. Answers 503 when any dependency is unusable so that traffic is withheld rather than sent into failure.

Codecs, in the order chdman should try them. Omitted, chdman's
defaults for the transformation.

`chd_create_cd`, `chd_create_dvd`, `cue_bin_from_ccd` (a CUE/BIN of a

Must be `true`. Erasing destroys everything on the disc in the drive,
and the request has to say that this is intended.

`quick`, which does only what makes the disc writable again, or
`full`, which writes over the whole disc. Quick is fast on a CD-RW;
some drives erase a whole DVD-RW either way, which takes half an hour
or more. Full can take an hour.

asked for with `POST /artifacts/{id}/validate`.

RequestRip.description:
What an operator sends to rip the disc in a drive. Every field is
optional: `{}` rips without decryption, a CD with the worker's best tool.

The tool to read a CD with (ADR 0015): `redumper`, which corrects the
drive's read offset and needs a worker built with it, or `cdrdao`,
which every worker has. Absent: redumper where the drive's worker has
it, cdrdao elsewhere. Ignored for a disc that is not a CD.

Decrypt the disc if it is encrypted (ADR 0013). Needs an
administrator to have turned decryption on, and the drive's worker
to run an image built to decrypt.

When decrypting, the original to keep: `encrypted_original` (the
default: the disc as it is, with a decrypted copy beside it) or
`decrypted_original` (only a decrypted image, not a faithful copy of
the disc). Ignored without `decrypt`.
